name_note: Published work uses the name Phascolarctobacterium succinatutens; in GTDB these genomes fall in Phascolarctobacterium_A succinatutens_B, one of several GTDB species split from that named species, so published findings may cover a broader group.

sentences.text: Phascolarctobacterium succinatutens is a bacterium of the human gut whose abundance has been measured in stool metagenomes.
A study using Norwegian cohorts and curatedMetagenomicData reported that positive associations with adenomas and colorectal cancer were verified for Phascolarctobacterium succinatutens.
The same study reported that men show a higher prevalence of P. succinatutens across cohorts, and that its pangenome was enriched for genes related to porphyrin metabolism.
In pigs, a study reported Phascolarctobacterium succinatutens as a key bacterium with greater abundance in animals with low backfat thickness, and administration in mice curbed weight gain.
